4 · Architecture

12 files, 181 lines · React, Vite. 7 entry points: the places a user, a request, or a command can start running code.

  • route GET /users/{user_id} shop/app.py
  • route POST /backup shop/app.py
  • cli click.command() shop/cli.py
  • main python shop/cli.py shop/cli.py
  • main app start (web/src/main.tsx) web/src/main.tsx
  • page /admin web/src/pages/Admin.tsx
  • page /users/:id web/src/pages/UserPage.tsx

2 of 3 frontend HTTP calls are linked to a backend route in this repo; 1 go to external services.

Recommended deployment

  • Deploy the frontend and the API as two pieces: the frontend as static files or on a platform such as Vercel or Netlify, the API as a container (Fly.io, Render, Railway, Cloud Run).
  • Keep all configuration in environment variables, with an .env.example listing every name.
  • Use a managed database with automatic backups, and connect through a pooled connection string.
  • Put the API behind HTTPS only, and allow your frontend's origin in CORS (not `*`).

Protections to add (4)

Heuristic: shown only where the code gives a reason; they don't change findings or the score.

addRate limiting
1 route(s) that change data can be called as fast as an attacker likes: password guessing, sign-up spam, or running up your bill.
Evidence: POST /backup (shop/app.py:14)
Limit requests per user and per IP on these routes: slowapi (FastAPI), Flask-Limiter, express-rate-limit, or @upstash/ratelimit (Next.js / serverless).
addSecurity headers
Browsers protect your users from clickjacking, mixed content, and injected scripts only when the app sends headers such as Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, and X-Frame-Options.
Evidence: full-stack web app; no header setup found in code or hosting config
Set them once for every response: helmet (Express), the headers() block in next.config.js, a vercel.json/netlify.toml headers rule, or a small middleware in FastAPI/Flask.
addSlow password hashing
Passwords are handled in the code, and a fast hash (MD5/SHA) is used in the same files: a leaked database could be cracked in hours.
Evidence: shop/auth.py:18
Store only argon2 or bcrypt hashes (passlib/pwdlib/bcrypt in Python, bcrypt or argon2 in Node), or use a managed auth service so you never store passwords.
addLogin check on routes that change data
1 route(s) change data with no sign of a login check in the handler, in what it calls, or in app-wide middleware, so anyone on the internet can call them.
Evidence: POST /backup (shop/app.py:14)
Check the signed-in user at the top of each handler (or in shared middleware), and check they may act on this record, not just that they are signed in.

1 more finding(s) are in test code only.

8 · Limits · what this report does not prove

  • Business-logic flaws. Scanners and graph checks find known patterns; they can't tell whether your rules (who may see what, what a price should be) are right.
  • Calls Lantern could not trace. 6 call sites were left unresolved rather than guessed, mostly calls into libraries or very dynamic code (getattr, plugins, hooks returning objects).
  • Runtime behavior. No code was run for this report, so every edge is from static analysis and tests were not executed.
  • Frontend call edges are static only (no JavaScript runtime tracing yet).
  • npm dependencies were not fully checked for known vulnerabilities (skipped: no package-lock.json, so exact versions are unknown (commit your lock file)).
  • 1 finding is from heuristic checks that can misfire; they are labeled as such.
  • The readiness score uses file and pattern checks. A check passing means the thing exists, not that it is configured well.
